title: SAP Fiori: SmartControls (sap.ui.comp)
tags: fiori, smart controls, ui comp, table, form
excerpt: Smart Controls — semi-automatic UI based on OData metadata.
body:
## SmartControls
Controls que auto-generan UI basado en OData annotations:
- SmartTable
- SmartForm
- SmartField
- SmartFilterBar
- SmartVariantManagement

Middle ground entre Fiori Elements (100% auto) y freestyle (100% custom).

## SmartTable
```xml
<smart:SmartTable xmlns:smart='sap.ui.comp.smarttable'
    entitySet='Products'
    tableType='ResponsiveTable'
    useExportToExcel='true'
    useVariantManagement='true'
    header='Productos'/>
```

Columns auto-derived from `UI.LineItem` annotation.

### Config
- `entitySet` — OData collection
- `tableType` — ResponsiveTable / Table / TreeTable / AnalyticalTable
- `useExportToExcel` — botón export
- `useVariantManagement` — save/load variants
- `enableAutoBinding` — auto load on filter

## SmartFilterBar
```xml
<smart:SmartFilterBar entitySet='Products' persistencyKey='myFilterKey' search='.onSearch'/>
```

Filter fields desde `UI.SelectionFields` annotation.

## SmartForm
```xml
<smart:SmartForm xmlns:smart='sap.ui.comp.smartform' editable='true'>
    <smart:Group label='General'>
        <smart:GroupElement>
            <smart:SmartField value='{Name}'/>
        </smart:GroupElement>
        <smart:GroupElement>
            <smart:SmartField value='{Price}'/>
        </smart:GroupElement>
    </smart:Group>
</smart:SmartForm>
```

Field labels + types from OData metadata.

## SmartField
Auto-renderer basado en OData type:
- Text → Input
- Boolean → CheckBox
- Date → DatePicker
- Currency → Currency-formatted Input
- Foreign key → ComboBox con value help

## Ventajas
- Menos código para CRUD standard
- Metadata-driven → cambios en backend auto-reflected
- Consistent behavior across app

## Desventajas
- Menos flexible que freestyle
- Debugging más complex
- Deprecated en favor de Fiori Elements V4

## Migration
SAP recomienda mover a Fiori Elements V4 para nuevos proyectos. SmartControls todavía suportados pero less investment.

## Common issues
- **Columns wrong** — annotations missing
- **Filter empty** — SelectionFields not defined
- **Value help slow** — restrict value help query

title: SAP Fiori: draft handling
excerpt: Auto-save de borradores en Fiori Elements.
body:
## Contexto
Draft = borrador. Changes guardados provisionally antes de commit (activate).

Beneficios:
- Auto-save (no perder trabajo)
- Preview antes de publicar
- Multiple usuarios pueden ver draft co-editar
- Optimistic locking (draft creates lock)

## Enable draft en backend (CDS)
```cds
entity Products : cuid, managed {
    key ID: Integer;
    name: String(100);
    price: Decimal(10,2);
}

entity Products @(
    Common.SemanticKey: [ID],
    Common.DraftRoot: { ActivationAction: 'CatalogService.EntityContainer/activate' }
);
```

CAP genera automatic draft tables + APIs.

## Draft flow (user perspective)
1. User opens entity in edit mode
2. **Fiori creates draft** (backend copy)
3. User modifies fields
4. Auto-save every 30 sec (or on unfocus)
5. User clicks **Save** → activates draft → becomes 'live' record
6. Or **Discard** → draft deleted, no changes

## Runtime behavior
### Auto-save indicator
'Draft saved 10 seconds ago' subtle text.

### Concurrency
Only one user can edit a record's draft at a time.

Other users see 'This record is being edited by X'.

### Recover draft
Si user closes browser, draft persists. Next login → 'Continue editing?' prompt.

## Discard
Explicit button:
```
Discard button → dialog 'Discard changes?' → confirm → draft removed
```

## Timeout
Draft expires after N days idle (config). Automatically discarded.

## Draft admin actions
Admin can list all drafts:
- Force discard old ones (cleanup)
- Reassign to another user

## Programmatic control
### Check if in draft mode
```javascript
var bIsDraft = this.getView().getBindingContext().getObject().IsActiveEntity === false;
```

### Trigger activate
```javascript
await this.getView().getModel().functionCall({
    functionName: 'CatalogService.EntityContainer/activate',
    urlParameters: { ... }
});
```

## Freestyle draft
For custom apps, implement manually:
- 'Save draft' button (state = 'draft')
- 'Publish' button (state = 'live')
- App logic filters by state

Más trabajo pero total control.

## Common issues
- **Draft won't save** — validation fails
- **Activate blocked** — required fields missing
- **Draft persists after refresh** — expected, feature
- **Two drafts for same record** — impossible; user prompted to overwrite or abort

## Best practices
- **Enable draft** para entidades editadas frecuentemente
- **Config timeout** conservador (7-30 días)
- **Notify users** de auto-save (UI indicator)
- **Cleanup jobs** para expired drafts

title: SAP Fiori: launchpad settings + user preferences
excerpt: Config personal de launchpad para usuarios.
body:
## User settings
Access vía launchpad → avatar top-right → **Settings**.

### Available sections
- **Appearance** — theme, language, RTL
- **User profile** — name, email, avatar
- **Home page** — start page config
- **Notifications** — enable/disable
- **Search** — enterprise search preferences
- **Spaces + Pages** — organize apps
- **Sign out**

## Theme selection
List: sap_horizon, sap_horizon_dark, sap_belize, sap_fiori_3, sap_horizon_hcb (high contrast).

Saved per user.

## Language
List available languages. Change → app reload.

RTL languages auto-mirror layout.

## Notifications
- Enable browser push
- Email digest
- Silence certain categories

## Spaces + Pages (moderno)
Hierarchical org:
- **Space** — top-level (My Home, Sales, HR)
- **Page** — within space
- **Section** — group of tiles within page

Users drag/drop tiles to organize.

## Classic groups (legacy)
- Home group
- Custom groups
- Move tiles between

Either Spaces/Pages OR groups, depending launchpad version.

## Reset personalization
Settings → **Reset personalization**:
- Clears user's customizations
- Reverts to catalog defaults

Useful si user made mess.

## Admin restrictions
Admin can lock certain personalization:
- Prevent theme change
- Prevent tile removal
- Prevent search

For kiosk-style deployments.

## Global settings vs user
Default settings apply first time user logs in. Then user overrides.

## Recent activities
Launchpad tracks:
- Recently opened apps
- Frequently used
- Favorites

Quick access in Home space.

## Save site config
Admin → Site Manager (BTP Work Zone) → publish site changes.

Users see new site on next login.

## Search
### Enterprise search integration
Admin configures data sources:
- Business objects (SAP data)
- Content (documents)
- Apps

Users search across everything from launchpad search bar (Ctrl+K).

### Type-ahead
As user types, suggestions appear.

## App Finder
Search/browse all apps user has access to (unpinned).
User can pin to their homepage.

## Diagnostics
`#Shell-diag` → diagnostic screen for launchpad issues.

## Common issues
- **Setting not persisting** — cookies blocked
- **Language not changing** — bookmark URL has language param overriding
- **Theme flicker** — cache issue, hard refresh

## Mobile
SAP Mobile Start app respects user settings. Automatic sync.

SAP Fiori: search y enterprise search integration
excerpt: Enterprise search integrado en Fiori launchpad.
body:
## Enterprise Search
Cross-system search desde launchpad (Ctrl+K).

Searches:
- Business objects (SAP data — customers, orders, materials)
- Apps
- Content (documents)
- Users

## Componentes

### Search connector
Backend service que indexa data sources.

### Search UI
Launchpad search bar + result page.

## Config

### S/4HANA embedded search
- ESH (Enterprise Search) service
- Configure providers en `ESH_ADMIN`

### BTP
- SAP HANA Enterprise Search service

## Adding data source
1. Admin → **Search Configuration**
2. New provider:
   - Type: OData / API / Document store
   - Endpoint
   - Indexed fields
3. Save + activate index

## Custom search integration
Apps expose search via OData:
```xml
<Property Name='ID' Type='Edm.String' searchable='true'/>
<Property Name='Description' Type='Edm.String' searchable='true'/>
```

Register endpoint en launchpad config.

## Search UI within app
Component `sap.m.SearchField`:
```xml
<SearchField placeholder='Search products...' search='.onSearch' liveChange='.onLiveSearch'/>
```

```javascript
onSearch: function(oEvent) {
    var query = oEvent.getParameter('query');
    this._filterList(query);
},

onLiveSearch: function(oEvent) {
    // Debounced
    clearTimeout(this._searchTimer);
    this._searchTimer = setTimeout(() => this._doSearch(oEvent), 300);
}
```

## Search filters (advanced)
Use `sap.ui.model.Filter`:
```javascript
var aFilters = [];
if (searchTerm) {
    aFilters.push(new Filter([
        new Filter('Name', FilterOperator.Contains, searchTerm),
        new Filter('Description', FilterOperator.Contains, searchTerm)
    ], false));  // OR
}

var oBinding = this.byId('table').getBinding('items');
oBinding.filter(aFilters);
```

## Global search vs local
- **Global (launchpad)** — across all systems + apps
- **Local (app-level)** — within current app's data

## Results ranking
- Relevance (matched fields, tokens)
- Recency
- User personalization (based on their past clicks)

## Deep link
User clicks result → navigate to app with pre-filled context:
```
#Product-display?ProductID=123&highlight=widget
```

App receives + highlights widget in results.

## Analytics
Search analytics available for admins:
- Top queries
- No-results queries → gaps to fill
- Click-through rates

## Common issues
- **Search returns no results** — index stale or missing
- **Slow search** — index size too large, optimize provider
- **Wrong results** — data source needs re-indexing

## SmartFilterBar en apps
Many Fiori apps use SmartFilterBar (`sap.ui.comp.smartfilterbar.SmartFilterBar`):
- Auto-generated from OData metadata
- Advanced filter UI (date ranges, value help)
- Variant management

title: SAP Fiori: OData batch requests
excerpt: Combinar múltiples OData ops en un solo HTTP request.
body:
## Batch requests
Múltiples OData operations en 1 HTTP request → reduces round-trips.

## OData v2 batch
```
POST /sap/opu/odata/sap/API/$batch HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=BOUNDARY

--BOUNDARY
Content-Type: application/http

GET /Products(1) HTTP/1.1

--BOUNDARY
Content-Type: application/http

GET /Customers(100) HTTP/1.1

--BOUNDARY--
```

## SAPUI5 v2 model automatic batch
```javascript
var oModel = new sap.ui.model.odata.v2.ODataModel(url, {
    useBatch: true,
    defaultBindingMode: 'TwoWay'
});

// These 3 calls will be batched into 1 HTTP request
oModel.read('/Products(1)');
oModel.read('/Customers(100)');
oModel.read('/Orders(50)');
// Batch submitted en next event loop
```

## Change sets (transactions)
Multiple write ops as atomic:
```
--BOUNDARY
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=CHANGESET

--CHANGESET
Content-Type: application/http

POST /Products HTTP/1.1

--CHANGESET
Content-Type: application/http

PATCH /Products(1) HTTP/1.1

--CHANGESET--
--BOUNDARY--
```

All succeed or all rollback.

### SAPUI5 v2
```javascript
oModel.setDeferredGroups(['myGroup']);

oModel.create('/Products', { name: 'A' }, { groupId: 'myGroup' });
oModel.update('/Products(1)', { price: 100 }, { groupId: 'myGroup' });

oModel.submitChanges({ groupId: 'myGroup' });
// All grouped into 1 changeset
```

## OData v4
Batch handled more transparently. Use `submitBatch`:
```javascript
await oModel.submitBatch('mainGroup');
```

Model groups changes automatically.

## Performance benefits
- 1 HTTP request vs N
- Less overhead (headers, TCP handshakes)
- Faster user experience

### Batch de 10 requests
- Sin batch: 10 * 100 ms = 1 sec (with network + backend)
- Con batch: ~200 ms (backend processes all, single response)

## Cuándo NO usar batch
- Single request (no benefit)
- Streaming responses
- Very large payloads (multiple MB) — may hit limits

## Debugging batch
Browser DevTools:
- Network tab → filter for `$batch`
- Inspect request/response
- Multi-part parsing tools help

## Backend support
- **S/4HANA + newer OData** — full batch support
- **Older systems** — may not support changesets

Check OData service metadata.

## Rate limiting
Batch = 1 HTTP request. If rate-limited per HTTP call, batches count as 1. Beneficial.

But backend may still limit total operations.

## Errors within batch
Some requests succeed, others fail:
- v2: each response has its own status code
- v4: transactional semantics stricter

Handle per-request en response parser.

## Best practices
- **Enable batch** for OData v2 (`useBatch: true`)
- **Group related ops** in changesets for atomicity
- **Don't over-batch** — too many ops in one may timeout
- **Monitor size** — server may enforce max batch size

title: SAP Fiori: SAP Fiori Tools (VS Code extension)
excerpt: Extensiones VS Code para dev Fiori.
body:
## SAP Fiori tools
Pack de extensiones VS Code para desarrollo Fiori:
- **Application Generator** — create Fiori apps
- **Service Modeler** — visual OData design
- **Guided Development** — best practice suggestions
- **XML Toolkit** — XML view validation
- **App Modeler** — visual manifest editor

## Install
VS Code marketplace: 'SAP Fiori tools - Extension Pack'.

## Application Generator
### Create Fiori app
1. Command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) → **Fiori: Open Application Generator**
2. Choose template (List Report, Object Page, etc.)
3. Choose data source (OData v2/v4, local mock)
4. Configure app ID, description, launchpad target
5. Generate

Same templates que BAS wizard, en VS Code local.

## Service Modeler
Edit OData annotations con visual UI.

### Open
Right-click annotations file → **Show Service Modeler**.

### Modify
- Add UI.LineItem entries
- Add UI.FieldGroup
- Configure semantic keys

Saves back to annotations XML.

## Guided Development
Menu **Fiori: Open Guided Development**:
- List of common tasks (add filter, add action, etc.)
- Step-by-step instructions
- Code snippets inserted

Good for learning.

## App preview
```bash
npm start
```

Opens local server + preview browser. Hot reload on file changes.

### Preview con mock data
```bash
npm run start-mock
```

Mock OData server (no backend needed).

### Preview con destination BTP
```bash
npm run start-noflp
```

Uses `.env` con destination config.

## Debug
1. VS Code → **Run and Debug** (F5)
2. Configuration 'Launch Fiori App'
3. Chrome opens with debugger attached
4. Set breakpoints en controller JS

## Deploy from VS Code
### To ABAP repository
```bash
npm run deploy
```

### To BTP
```bash
npm run build
cf deploy mta_archives/*.mtar
```

## Local mock server
`mockdata/` folder:
```
mockdata/
    Products.json
    Customers.json
    metadata.xml
```

Mock backend for development sin backend real.

## Fiori Elements editing
Special editor para Fiori Elements pages:
- Visual editor
- Add sections, columns
- Real-time preview

## Comparación BAS vs VS Code + Fiori tools
- **BAS**: cloud IDE, integrated con BTP, no local install
- **VS Code**: local, full control, extensive marketplace

Both support same Fiori workflows. Choose based on preference.

## Command-line alternatives
Even without VS Code, use CLIs:
```bash
npx @sap/generator-fiori
npx fiori generate
```

## Common issues
- **Templates fail** — Node.js version wrong (need 18+)
- **npm install slow** — SAP registry
- **Debug not connecting** — port conflict

## Best practices
- **Fiori tools pack** — install full extension pack
- **Latest Node.js LTS**
- **Sync frequently** with team (via Git)
- **Test builds** en CI before merge

title: SAP Fiori: launchpad launchpad content publish (BTP)
excerpt: Publicar apps al launchpad de BTP Work Zone.
body:
## BTP Work Zone
Successor de Launchpad Service. Es el launchpad moderno.

## Subscribe
Subaccount → **Subscriptions → SAP Build Work Zone, standard/advanced edition**.

## Deploy Fiori app
### Requirements
- MTA project
- HTML5 app module
- xsuaa binding
- html5-apps-repo binding

### mta.yaml
```yaml
ID: my-fiori-app
version: 1.0.0
modules:
    - name: approuter
      type: approuter.nodejs
      requires:
          - name: xsuaa-service
          - name: html5-apps-repo
    - name: ui
      type: html5
      path: ui
resources:
    - name: xsuaa-service
      type: org.cloudfoundry.managed-service
      parameters:
          service: xsuaa
          service-plan: application
    - name: html5-apps-repo
      type: org.cloudfoundry.managed-service
      parameters:
          service: html5-apps-repo
          service-plan: app-host
```

### Deploy
```bash
mbt build
cf deploy mta_archives/*.mtar
```

App uploaded to HTML5 Applications repo.

## Register en Work Zone
1. BTP cockpit → **Build Work Zone** subscription → **Open**
2. **Content Manager** → **New**
3. Select **Business App**
4. Provide:
    - App name
    - Description
    - Semantic Object
    - Action
    - URL (path to app en HTML5 repo)
    - Icon

5. Save

## Add to catalog
### Catalog
Group de apps logically:
1. Content Manager → **New → Business Catalog**
2. Name: 'Sales Apps'
3. Add apps to catalog

### Group
1. New → **Business Group**
2. Add catalogs to group

## Site
Portal / launchpad site users see:
1. Site Manager → **New Site**
2. Add spaces + pages
3. Assign catalogs
4. Assign role collections (who can access)
5. Publish

## User access
Users with assigned role collection:
1. Access site URL
2. Login via XSUAA
3. See tiles from catalogs assigned

## Multiple sites
Different user groups may need different views:
- Sales site
- Finance site
- Ops site

Each with own catalogs + branding.

## Themes
Custom themes via Theme Designer.
Assign per site.

## Content types
- **HTML5 app** (Fiori)
- **URL link** (external site)
- **SAP Fiori launchpad content** (from Fiori 3 launchpad)
- **News** (advanced edition)
- **Cards**

## Cross-navigation
App A → App B via intents (semantic object + action).

Register inbounds/outbounds en manifest.

## Common issues

### 'Tile not visible'
- Role not assigned
- Catalog not en site

### 'App broken after deploy'
- HTML5 repo binding stale
- Redeploy

### 'CORS'
- Backend not configured
- Or destination properties missing

## Migration from Launchpad service
Work Zone Standard offers similar. Advanced adds:
- News
- Company communication
- Custom content

SAP publishes migration guide.

title: SAP Fiori: launchpad admin — managing users at scale
excerpt: Config launchpad para muchos usuarios y roles.
body:
## Escenario
Org con 1000+ usuarios. Multiple business units. Diverse roles.

## Role management

### Business roles (S/4HANA)
Pre-delivered:
- SAP_BR_EMPLOYEE
- SAP_BR_MANAGER
- SAP_BR_ACCOUNTANT
- SAP_BR_SALES_REPRESENTATIVE
- Etc.

Custom roles copy + modify these.

### Assign
`SU01` per user + PFCG:
- Slow for bulk

### Bulk
`SU10` — mass user modification.

### AD group integration
SAML/OIDC federation:
- User's AD group → SAP role auto-assigned
- Central management via AD

## Catalog structure
### Standard catalogs
SAP delivers 100s of catalogs (per business function).

### Custom catalog
Combine tiles logically:
- FI-A/R Reports
- FI-A/P Postings
- Vendor Management

## Groups
Users see groups en Home space:
- Home (default)
- Custom groups per role

## Space + Page (moderno)
### Space
Top-level (My Home, Sales, HR).

### Page
Within space, custom layout of tiles.

Admin defines defaults. Users personalize.

## Central user administration (CUA)
Multi-system landscape:
- 1 central system holds user master data
- Propagates to satellite systems (S/4, BW, CRM)

Avoid managing users in each system separately.

## Automatic provisioning

### From HR
S/4HANA HCM triggers:
- New employee → auto-create SAP user
- Termination → auto-deactivate

### From AD via CUA
AD as source of truth. Sync to SAP.

### IPS (Identity Provisioning Service - BTP)
Cloud-based sync:
- AD → BTP IAS → all connected SAP systems

## Onboarding checklist
1. AD account created
2. Group memberships in AD (drives SAP roles)
3. S/4HANA user provisioned
4. Fiori launchpad access verified
5. First-login training scheduled

## Offboarding checklist
1. Deactivate SAP user (SU01)
2. Remove AD groups
3. Transfer ownership of workflows/approvals
4. Data retention per policy

## Access review
Quarterly review:
- Users with SAP_ALL — verify still needed
- Inactive users — deactivate
- Role escalation — check

SuiCLI + reports.

## Auditing (SM19/SM20)
Log:
- Login attempts
- Role changes
- Sensitive transaction access

SIEM integration.

## Common patterns

### Per-role provisioning
For each new user, admin picks:
- Employment type (permanent, contractor)
- Job function (sales, finance, warehouse)

→ auto-assigned role bundle.

### Time-limited access
```sql
End date en user master → auto-lock
```

Contractors get expiration.

### Emergency access
Break-glass account:
- SAP_ALL role
- Password vaulted, requires management approval
- All actions audited
- Reset password after use

## Fiori launchpad ownership
- Business role owner: business team
- Technical role owner: IT security
- Regular sync meetings

## KPIs
- Provisioning cycle time (target: <4h from hire)
- Deprovisioning delay (target: same day termination)
- Access anomalies (target: 0)

## Best practices
- **Automate** onboarding/offboarding
- **Regular audits** — quarterly
- **Documentation** — role catalog with descriptions
- **Training** — new users get standard onboarding
- **Feedback loop** — users report missing access quickly
